partners.next_step: Use published landlord route (p3housing@p3charity.org) to ask whether Gloucestershire intake is open, whether 5–30-unit portfolios qualify, and request contracting-entity details, full draft lease and current financial statements before underwriting. No enquiry sent.
risks: Published 6–12-month duration is a mismatch for investors seeking long contracted income.
National landlord invitation does not verify local portfolio demand.
Marketing language about risk-free letting is not a substitute for lease and covenant due diligence.
Confirm permitted use, planning, licensing, insurance and commissioning/support arrangements for each asset.

partners.region: Cheltenham-based; Gloucestershire including Cheltenham, Gloucester, Stroud, Tewkesbury, Forest of Dean and Cotswolds; wider South West and West Midlands.
partners.type: Supported-accommodation and homelessness charity; RSH registered-provider status not verified

property_criteria.published: FY2024 audited trustees report says accommodation managed ranges from houses/flats suitable for 1–3 people through larger sites accommodating 20+ people in individual and shared self-contained homes; accommodation is CCP-owned, leased or operated under a management agreement.
property_criteria.portfolio_fit: Historical operating model is directly relevant to an investor-owned supported-accommodation portfolio, but not an invitation to submit 5–30 units and not evidence of current intake.
not_published: Accepted locations and current commissioned need

coverage_evidence.date: Live service pages checked 2026-10-19; operating-model evidence FY ended 2024-03-31
coverage_evidence.scope: Official Gloucestershire vulnerable-adults page names all six Gloucestershire districts and shared houses/self-contained flats. Page contains inconsistent age wording (18+ in introduction, 18–25 elsewhere); confirm intended cohort. Head office is 340 High Street, Cheltenham GL50 3JF.

covenant_evidence.scope: Current Charity Commission full record reports income £12,981,517, expenditure £12,428,309, own-use assets £6.73m, other assets £2.82m and liabilities £7.02m. £6,203,830 income is from 28 government contracts. These are charity-level reported financial figures, not a rental guarantee or lease-specific credit opinion.
covenant_evidence.limitations: Headline register figures do not establish unrestricted liquidity, covenant headroom, contract renewal security or capacity for a new 5–30-unit commitment. Obtain full current accounts and management information.

regulator_evidence.scope: Charity Commission registration 1043143 and company identity verified. No RSH registration or current RSH G/V/C judgement verified for CCP in this research. Do not present charity status or reported housing activity as RSH approval.

partners.next_step: Ask CCP housing/partnership leadership, via main published contact 0300 365 8999 or ccphelpdesk@ccp.org.uk, whether new investor-owned leased or managed properties are sought in the target district; request cohort, commissioner, specification, legal counterparty and draft terms. No outreach made.
risks: Historical leasing/management evidence does not prove current landlord intake.
Support contract funding and property lease obligations may have different durations.
Do not confuse dormant historic CCP Homes subsidiary with the operating charity or assume it provides an RP covenant.
Official vulnerable-adults service age criteria need clarification.

coverage_evidence.date: RSH judgement 2026-10-07; official ESG report 2023 for more granular historic locations
coverage_evidence.scope: RSH confirms GSA operates in 36 local authority areas across West Midlands, Oxfordshire, Gloucestershire and Wiltshire and owns/manages about 25,500 social homes. covenant_evidence.date: 2026-10-07, RSH investigation; financial deterioration includes FY ended 2026-03-31
covenant_evidence.scope: RSH states GSA has weak financial performance, losses, weak interest cover and poor forecasting. Although lender covenants had not been breached, compliance depends on substantial disposals, cost reductions and transformation programmes. Limited capacity to absorb a reasonable range of adverse scenarios.
covenant_evidence.limitations: This is adverse group/provider viability evidence, not a lease guarantee. Do not use old G1/G2 or V2 grades as current underwriting evidence.

regulator_evidence.scope: Current RSH judgement for GreenSquareAccord Limited LH3902: G3/V3 downgraded, both non-compliant. C2 retained from October 2025 because consumer standards were not reassessed. Serious concerns: financial governance, risk management, information quality and controls; sustainable improvement not evidenced.

partners.next_step: Do not treat as a strong lease covenant merely because it is a large RP. If still considering a partnership, first establish current external-property intake appetite and obtain latest recovery-plan, liquidity and covenant evidence plus exact contracting entity; independent credit/legal review before any heads of terms. No outreach made.
risks: G3/V3 serious regulatory and financial concerns as of 7 October 2026.
Current covenant compliance relies on disposals and savings; it is not evidence of durable rental-payment security.
No private investor landlord intake verified.
General care/support capability and development partnerships do not establish management of investor-owned portfolios.
